limitations: The compressed candidate.2 tarball is not materialized in the bundle. Its receipt is present, and all 201 materialized members plus MANIFEST.json and SHA256SUMS were independently replayed.

The candidate.3 raw audit output and complete per-finding register are absent. The first two listed parent IDs are provisionally accounted as P0, the next six as P1, and the final four as P2 to preserve the only available 2/6/4 aggregate; this is not a recovered per-ID severity mapping.

The closed-set audit did not execute pytest, Ruff, a wheel rebuild, or a fresh installation because Runtime access was prohibited. It verified the retained captures, source, lock, wheel, RECORD, and report bindings.
The upstream BFCL checkout, model bytes, and host executables are not materialized. Their identities are therefore report-bound rather than independently byte-replayed.

findings.rationale: The bootstrap CLI accepts arbitrary caller-supplied stage-receipt and identity paths. _verify_stage_receipt checks self-declared fields and hashes only; it does not require the receipts to be outputs of import_dg10_candidate4_ai_audits, bind them to its aggregate receipt, or replay the two provider event streams. The authorization test hand-writes policy, identity, evidence, and ACCEPTED AI_INDEPENDENT stage receipts and obtains authorized=true. The release gate reuses the same verifier, so an author can synthesize the trust root that is meant to be independent.
findings.required_action: Require fixed importer-produced aggregate and stage receipts. At authorization and release, replay their two distinct xhigh AI run receipts and raw-event bindings, and reject standalone caller-selected stage receipts.
findings.title: Caller-authored stage receipts can mint bootstrap and release authority

findings.rationale: build_quality_gate accepts a hand-authored milai.dg10.ai-test-access-approval.v1 object after checking only self-declared candidate, decision, authority, policy hash, open counts, input hashes, and evidence paths. It does not validate a dedicated importer, provider thread, raw-event/output binding, model, or xhigh reasoning. The unit test writes arbitrary one-line AI evidence and this approval and expects full_test_authorized=true. This makes protected full-test access author-mintable.
findings.required_action: Introduce a dedicated immutable AI test-access importer and require the gate to replay its provider events, output, model, xhigh reasoning, bundle identity, and independent receipt provenance before granting the single full-test access.
findings.title: A hand-authored AI approval can authorize protected full-test access

findings.rationale: The acceptance contract requires exactly 24 T2 calls and all attempts to be preallocated and ledgered. smoke_preflight merely supplies integer 24 to evaluate_first_model_authorization. AttemptLedger.start_attempt can mint unbounded one-call attempts and enforces only per-record chaining and shape. The T2 gate checks call_count=24 after execution; no adapter consumes one immutable preallocated slot before a provider call. Authorization therefore does not technically constrain the next phase to exactly 24 calls.
findings.required_action: Preallocate exactly 24 immutable call-slot IDs in the authorization artifact, require atomic consumption of one unused bound slot before every provider call, forbid additional attempts, and reconcile all slots and outcomes before any later gate.
findings.title: The exact 24-call bootstrap budget is neither preallocated nor enforced at call time

findings.rationale: The worker-closure report commits 324 runner entries and includes runtime/migrations/script.py.mako with SHA-256 d3244c86d221281de16e369b51c24857af6569d93d7dd65564591c618da8498a and size 594. That file is absent from current-source, the 365-entry source inventory, and the review manifest. Independent set and hash replay found it as the only worker entry absent from current source. The claimed imported source/config closure is therefore not the materialized source identity, even though the retained wheel and captures hash correctly.
findings.required_action: Materialize the exact runtime/migrations/script.py.mako byte committed by the worker closure, include it in the source inventory and review manifest, then regenerate identities, rebuild the wheel, reinstall freshly, and rerun pytest and Ruff captures.
findings.title: The asserted worker source closure contains a file absent from candidate.4 source identity

findings.rationale: The immutable reasoning amendment and active candidate.4 audit runner require xhigh, but the candidate.4 acceptance contract still declares reasoning_effort=max and the contract validator does not reject that stale value. codex_sol_max.md also retains the old max instruction. The active path follows the superseding amendment, but the frozen policy surface is internally contradictory and validation reports PASS without detecting it.
findings.required_action: Issue a successor acceptance contract that explicitly binds the immutable xhigh amendment and update validation to fail on any effective model or reasoning mismatch; retire or clearly supersede the stale max instruction.
findings.title: The acceptance contract and validator retain a stale max-reasoning requirement

findings.rationale: The wheel-build capture records a temporary output path and successful build but not the rebuilt artifact's SHA-256, and the temporary wheel is not retained. The report asserts that the independent rebuilt digest equals 882b2f9d13fb16a2a756c21e73d3758789c1f5084129cdef3ae349ca4c8cb773, but the closed bundle contains only the referenced source wheel. The auditor can validate the shipped wheel and every RECORD row but cannot independently compare the claimed rebuilt bytes.
findings.required_action: Retain the independently rebuilt wheel in the closed bundle, or retain a manifest-bound capture that computes its SHA-256 before deletion and binds that digest to the build inputs and fresh-install receipt.
findings.title: The independent wheel rebuild is asserted but its rebuilt bytes or hash capture are absent

DG10-R0.rationale: All 201 materialized historical members exactly match the R0 member report; MANIFEST has 198 payload entries, SHA256SUMS covers all 200 non-self members, control hashes bind to the receipt, and the historical decision remains immutable NO_GO. Candidate succession is documented. R0 is nevertheless not semantically closed because the candidate.3 receipt omits the complete per-finding register required to re-evaluate and close DG10-C3-AI-001 through 012.

DG10-R1.rationale: Stage-qualified claims and current deny-state documents are materially improved, and the active audit path enforces xhigh. R1 fails because caller-authored AI/stage receipts can create bootstrap and release authority, a self-declared AI test-access receipt can authorize one full test, and the 24-call bootstrap is not preallocated or enforced at call time. The stale max requirement is an additional policy contradiction.

DG10-R2.rationale: The locked wheel hash is 882b2f9d13fb16a2a756c21e73d3758789c1f5084129cdef3ae349ca4c8cb773; its ZIP paths and all RECORD hashes and sizes validate. The retained captures hash correctly and report a fresh install, import probe, 203 passing tests, and Ruff success. R2 still fails because runtime/migrations/script.py.mako is committed by the 324-entry worker closure but absent from current-source and its 365-entry inventory. The claimed independent rebuild also lacks retained rebuilt bytes or a build-time digest capture, while upstream BFCL and model bytes remain report-bound.
